correctness.rationale: In cubic GP(8,3) every legal three-edge-colouring is an ordered triple of disjoint perfect matchings covering 24 edges. Least-unmatched-vertex branching exhausts 33 perfect matchings and yields 120 complete ordered partitions. For each state and colour pair, every alternating-cycle component is traversed and flipped once; deduplicating legal undirected switches gives exactly 342 edges and BFS components of 24 and 96 states. Independent direct perfect-matching enumeration and all-edge move construction confirmed degree histograms, edge counts, distance spheres, component diameters, bipartite status and odd girth. Four explicit original vertex automorphisms generate 96 permutations; their action on a large-component reference colouring has trivial stabilizer and is transitive, with six neighbor elements involutions, giving the Cayley structure. The 24-state component has the exhibited 5-cycle and no triangles. This enumeration is exhaustive for one finite graph, not an extrapolation to all cubic graphs.

value.rationale: The edge-Kempe reconfiguration graph is a natural combinatorial object in edge-colouring equivalence. Exact component metric, parity, cycle-signature and regular Cayley geometry reveal structural distinction beyond prior yes/no equivalence or order-wise census and furnish a reproducible benchmark for switching dynamics.

final_claim: For proper edge-colourings of GP(8,3) in three named colours under complete alternating bichromatic cycle switches, the reconfiguration graph has 120 states and 342 edges, components of sizes 24 (54 edges) and 96 (288 edges) with exact radii, diameters, cycle-factor signatures; the large component is a bipartite six-regular Cayley graph on a 96-element automorphism group.
